title: Vancouver · Sea to Sky and Duffey Lake
slogan: Coast mountains, fast weather and a proper Canadian day.
story: Coast mountains, fast weather and a proper Canadian day. Out of Squamish and back again: 321 km, roughly 5 h 32 in the saddle. The stops in between: Whistler, Pemberton and Duffey Lake Road. The highest point is about 1,600 m. Back roads rather than main roads, where the map allows.

sections.advice: Use Vancouver start → Squamish fuel as clean positioning. Keep it tidy, ignore impatient traffic and save the enthusiasm for the good road ahead. The value here is not drama; it is arriving at the riding section with space, fuel and concentration intact.

sections.advice: Whistler food → Pemberton is the logistics leg. Watch junctions, villages and speed changes, then let the roadbook do its job: move you out of the clutter without spending your best attention too early.

sections.advice: Pemberton → Duffey Lake Road is the reward section in Vancouver. Look through the bends, use legal pull-offs for photos and keep a little margin for tractors, cyclists and damp shade. The best ride here is smooth, not noisy.

scenicChapters.title: Sea-to-Sky Highway
scenicChapters.narrative: For 42 km this is Sea-to-Sky Highway, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it — expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast.

scenicChapters.title: Duffey Lake Road
scenicChapters.narrative: Water arrives beside the road and stays for 41 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go. Slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did.
